newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index down with focus on new issues.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index down with focus on new issues.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares inched down on Wednesday as investors turned away from the overall market and looked to buy new share issues, brokers said.

Newcomer Shanghai Zhenhua Port Machinery Co Ltd, which listed on Tuesday, stole the spotlight on Wednesday with investors continuing to buy the stock of the port machinery maker at the expense of other shares, brokers said.
The B index lost 0.178 points or 0.24 percent to 74.303 on volume of 23.944 million shares worth $9.841 million.
"There are no investors entering the market, except to buy new share issues," said an analyst at China Guotai Securities. "The market is weak because there is not enough capital."
Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal Co Ltd was to list 166 million B shares in Shanghai on Friday and investors were waiting for the new issue before entering the market to buy, brokers said.
A stellar peformance by the Hong Kong stock market has also drained capital away from the Shanghai bourse, they said.
"Everyone's attention seems to be focused on H shares in Hong Kong, so I don't expect much movement in the Shanghai market," said an analyst at a European securities firm.
H shares are shares of Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong.
Investors would look to new share issues and 1997 interim results in the short term for an excuse to re-enter the market, brokers said.
Yitai Coal, which lists on Friday, was not expected to debut as strongly as Zhenhua Port but was likely to put in a respectable performance despite troubles in the coal industry, they said.
Of 46 B shares, 42 traded with 17 down, 14 flat and 11 up.
Shanghai Post & Telecommunication Equipment Co was the biggest B share loser on talk of poor interim results. It slumped $0.022 or 6.67 percent to $0.308.
Zhenhua Port was the top gainer in the falling market and also the most actively traded B share. The stock soared $0.048 or 10 percent to $0.528 on volume of around 9.4 million shares.
Shanghai A shares tumbled late in the session on institutional selling amid cautious market sentiment, brokers said.
The A index fell 26.065 points or 2.08 percent to 1,225.801 points on volume of 266.361 million shares worth 2.788 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index lost 60.546 points or 1.62 percent to 3,687.487 points.
Rumours circulated once again on Wednesday that Shanghai Stock Exchange president, Yang Xianghai, would step down soon, brokers said.

Exchange officials and officials at the market watchdog agency, the China Securities Regulatory Commission, said they had received no official word of such a move. Similar speculation has been heard in the market in the past.
The A and B share markets were likely to register weak performances on Thursday with B share investors waiting for the Friday listing of Yitai Coal, brokers said.
